skill.name: clay-http-enrich
skill.description: Sets up a Clay HTTP API column that calls the Leadsets REST enrich endpoint to fill current role, company and verified work email for every row in a Clay table, tested on one row and paced against enrichment limits. Use when someone says "enrich my Clay table with Leadsets", "add Leadsets to Clay", "fill emails in Clay" or "Clay HTTP column for emails".
skill.summary: Enrich existing Clay contacts with Leadsets and track which work emails the service verifies.
skill.author: leadsets

security_audit.summary: No evidence found of shell execution, environment access, system reconnaissance, or prompt injection. The Leadsets MCP and REST workflows send contact identifiers to the provider, and the default scope can include every row with a blank email. The workflow marks rows as send-ready based on email verification alone, without checking outreach eligibility.

remediation.issue: A live probe and bulk run can proceed without explicit approval of the data transfer and row scope.
remediation.suggestion: Preview the destination, identifier fields, eligible row count, and estimated record use before any live request. Require approval for the probe and separate approval for the remaining rows.

remediation.issue: The Leadsets integration sends contact identifiers and authenticates REST requests using a stored bearer key.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict requests to the documented Leadsets endpoints and send only the identifiers needed for a match. Store the bearer key in Clay's secret store and redact it from logs and examples.

remediation.issue: Address verification alone controls membership in the send-ready view.
remediation.suggestion: Rename the view to Verified email and remove the sending recommendation. If keeping a send-ready view, require a separate outreach eligibility check and exclude suppressed contacts.

content.value_statement: Clay contact tables can contain missing job details and unverified work emails. This skill sets up Leadsets enrichment, separates email statuses, and sizes batches to your available records.
actual_capabilities: Checks Leadsets usage and reset times to plan batches within available limits.
Uses a live MCP probe to check whether the selected identifiers return the expected response.
Configures the Clay HTTP API column when access is available, or provides settings for manual setup.
Maps matched roles, companies, and work emails into Clay columns with verification status and a checked date.
Tests the mapping on ten rows and distinguishes verified, catch-all, unknown, and no-match outcomes.
Reports row outcomes, records used, and remaining quota.
limitations: Direct editing requires Clay access, and live requests require Leadsets credentials.
Existing contacts may return no match or an unconfirmed email. The skill does not find new contacts or return phone numbers.
Available records and rate limits can pause a run before it finishes.
The skill does not send email or add contacts to a sequencer. Verification alone does not establish outreach eligibility.

use_cases.title: Complete missing contact fields
use_cases.description: Use existing LinkedIn URLs to add current roles and companies to a Clay table. Keep email verification status visible for each match.

use_cases.title: Review client contact data before handoff
use_cases.description: Separate verified emails from catch-all and unknown results. Report no matches separately so clients know which rows still need review.

use_cases.title: Plan enrichment within account limits
use_cases.description: Compare the eligible row count with the available Leadsets records. Plan batches around the five-hour and weekly limits.

prompt_templates.title: Get manual setup settings
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: Plan the column without making live requests.
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to add a Leadsets HTTP API column in Clay using my LinkedIn URL column. Do not make any live requests.

prompt_templates.title: Check a single match
prompt_templates.scenario: Basic: Confirm that one approved test row returns the expected fields.
prompt_templates.prompt: Show the destination and identifier for one approved test row. After I confirm, run one Leadsets probe and summarize the match and email status.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a small batch
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Check mapped columns and status handling before a larger run.
prompt_templates.prompt: After I confirm, test the Leadsets column on ten approved rows. Check roles, companies, and email statuses, and report any no-match rows. Stop after the test.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a quota-aware rollout
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Run approved rows in stages and account for interruptions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check Leadsets usage and propose batches for approved rows with blank emails. Wait for approval before starting. Skip duplicates and report rows that need to resume.

output_examples.input: Test ten approved contacts and report the email status breakdown.
output: The ten-row test returned six verified emails, two catch-all results, one unknown result, and one no match.
The catch-all and unknown results stayed outside the verified view.

output_examples.input: Plan a run for 250 eligible rows when 100 records remain in this window.
output: Plan an initial batch of up to 100 rows.
Check usage after that batch and schedule the remaining rows after the window resets.

best_practices: Confirm which rows and identifier fields you can share with Leadsets before the first live request.
Store the API key in Clay's secret store and reuse the same idempotency key when retrying a request.
Check the mapping with a small batch and track outreach eligibility separately from email verification.
anti_patterns: Running all blank-email rows without reviewing the scope and available records.
Pasting the API key into a visible Clay cell or including it in a shared example.
Treating catch-all or unknown addresses as verified, or treating verified addresses as permission to send.

faq.question: What do I need to run this skill?
faq.answer: You need a Clay table, a Leadsets account, and a Leadsets API key for the HTTP column. The documented live probe uses MCP.

faq.question: What data is sent to Leadsets?
faq.answer: The request sends the mapped identifier fields, such as a LinkedIn URL or a full name with a company domain.

faq.question: Which rows does the skill select by default?
faq.answer: It selects rows with blank emails unless you specify a scope. Rows with verified emails and duplicate contacts are meant to be skipped.

faq.question: What happens when a request finds no match?
faq.answer: The row is marked as no match. The skill does not guess an address or retry the same row unchanged.

faq.question: What happens when a Leadsets limit is reached?
faq.answer: The workflow pauses or stops based on the limit and retry timing. The summary identifies which rows remain to run.

faq.question: Does the skill send email?
faq.answer: No. It updates Clay and reports email verification status. Check your outreach rules and suppression lists separately.
